subject: Climate & Environment
title: Storm Surge: The Silent Killer
description: A quick win: understand Storm Surge: The Silent Killer.

hook.text: Storm surge kills more people in hurricanes than wind, rain, or tornadoes combined.

buildup.text: Low pressure and strong winds push ocean water inland, creating a dome of water ahead of the storm.

discovery.text: Surge heights can exceed 6 meters — enough to submerge entire coastal towns.

twist.text: Hurricane Katrina's surge reached 8.5 meters in Mississippi, flooding areas 10 km from the coast.

climax.text: Climate change is raising sea levels, giving every future surge a higher starting point.

punchline.text: The deadliest part of a hurricane isn't the wind. It's the water.

quiz.question: What is storm surge?
options: A dome of ocean water pushed inland by the storm
A tsunami triggered by a hurricane

details.summary: Storm surge is a wall of ocean water pushed ashore by hurricane winds that can reach 6 meters or more above normal tide levels. It is the deadliest part of a tropical cyclone, responsible for roughly half of all hurricane fatalities in the United States historically.
details.whyItMatters: Storm surge kills more people than wind in most hurricanes. As sea levels rise, surges reach further inland, threatening ever-larger coastal populations.
takeaways: Surge heights can exceed 6 meters in major hurricanes
Low-lying coastal areas can be inundated within minutes
Sea-level rise adds to surge height, increasing future risk

faq.question: What determines how high storm surge will be?
faq.answer: Surge height depends on wind speed, storm size, approach angle, forward speed, coastal shape, and offshore depth. Shallow, gently sloping coastlines amplify surge far more than deep-water coasts with steep offshore drops.

faq.question: Why is storm surge more dangerous than hurricane wind?
faq.answer: Surge can inundate entire communities in minutes, trapping people in rising water with no time to escape. The force of moving water is immense, destroying structures wind alone would not, and carrying deadly debris.
